paper.title_en: Time optimal bang-bang control for dissipative superconducting N-level quantum systems
paper.abstract_en: This paper deals with time optimal control for dissipative superconducting N-level quantum systems. It involves minimizing the transition time from an initial state to a given final state. The minimum time is also called the quantum speed limit (QSL). In this case, the transition time is another control parameter. To solve this problem, we use automatic differentiation (AD). Dealing with the free target time requires a bounded optimal control. Depending on the bounded amplitude of the optimal control, the optimal solution may be bang-bang type, which switches often repetitively from the upper to the lower value of the control bounds. We also find singular arcs as optimal controls. Finding an accurate optimal protocol is a challenge because it is a dual objective optimization problem: one must minimize the deviation of the state of the system at the final time from the target state and simultaneously minimize the transition time. To overcome this difficulty we employ the penalty approach involving a Lagrange multiplier.[graphic not available: see fulltext] ,[graphic not available: see fulltext]
